name: Othership
who: Guided breathwork bathhouse chain (sauna, ice bath, communal ritual classes); day passes and memberships, four locations across Toronto and NYC/Brooklyn.
why: Defined the current group-breathwork-and-heat movement; devoted regular crowd and near-cult community culture.

name: Bathhouse
city: New York City (Williamsburg, Flatiron, Atlantic Ave)
who: Upscale communal bathhouse with saunas, steam, pools, and cold plunge; day pass and membership access, no invite needed.
why: The design-forward flagship of NYC's bathhouse boom, with the strongest regular scene and media footprint in the category.

name: SweatHouz
who: Franchised private-suite contrast therapy studio: infrared sauna, cold plunge, vitamin-C shower; book-by-suite, no membership required.
why: The fastest-scaling contrast-therapy franchise in the US, built for convenience over ritual.

name: SoJo Spa Club
who: Large-scale Korean-style spa and jjimjilbah with rooftop infinity pools facing Manhattan; day admission, no membership needed.
why: A purpose-built thermal resort at day-trip scale, with the biggest social reach of any US Korean-spa venue.

name: World Spa
who: 50,000-square-foot Korean-style spa near Coney Island with saunas, pools, and banya-style rooms; day pass access.
why: One of the largest purpose-built modern spa complexes in the US, drawing a citywide crowd, not just locals.

name: Remedy Place
city: New York City / Los Angeles / Boston
who: "Social wellness club" with ice baths, saunas, IV drips, NAD+, HBOT, and acupuncture in boutique clubs; bookable without membership.
why: Coined the social-wellness-club category and pulled it into celebrity culture, though breadth of services beats depth of any single ritual.

name: AIRE Ancient Baths
who: Candlelit thermal-bath circuit in a landmark building, recreating Roman/Ottoman bathing tradition; day pass and treatment bookings.
why: A new-build homage to ancient bathing with genuinely dramatic architecture, more special-occasion ritual than daily habit.

name: Restore Hyper Wellness
who: Franchised recovery-tech storefront chain: cryotherapy, IV drips, compression, red light, infrared sauna; pay-per-visit or membership.
why: The largest US recovery-tech franchise by location count, transactional rather than ritual or community-driven.

name: Sauna House
who: Nordic-style spa chain in repurposed historic buildings with sauna, cold plunge, and integrative massage; day pass and membership.
why: A well-reviewed Nordic thermal-journey format now franchising through the Southeast US.

name: Pause Studio
who: Recovery studio chain with private infrared sauna, float therapy, cold plunge, cryo, and IV drips across a growing US footprint.
why: A solid, expanding recovery-menu brand without a signature ritual or destination pull yet.

name: Nimbus Co
who: Infrared sauna and ice bath studio, Australia's first mover in the category (2016); communal rooms plus private suites across Sydney, Melbourne, and Byron Bay.
why: Beach-town founding brand of Australia's contrast-therapy scene, with genuine local community culture.

name: City Cave
who: Australia's largest float-therapy franchise: float tanks, infrared sauna, massage; pay-per-visit or membership at neighborhood centres.
why: The float-therapy category's scale leader in Australia, though individual sites are small suburban storefronts.

name: The Well
who: Members-first wellness club combining spa, integrative medical practice, and fitness studio; day visits bookable alongside membership.
why: A designed, membership-driven wellness club; broad medical-adjacent offering more than a focused heat/cold ritual.

name: The PEAQ Club
who: The Middle East's first social wellness club: ice baths, contrast therapy, HBOT, breathwork, and sound healing, built around shared/paired sessions; membership and day access.
why: Import of the social-wellness-club format into the Gulf, with a genuinely paired/communal design philosophy.

name: LUCA
who: Canal-side ice bath and sauna club with communal space, bar, and co-working area; day pass and membership.
why: A new, design-led entry in Amsterdam's growing ice-bath-and-sauna social scene, still building its reach.

name: Brooklyn Bathhouse
who: Neighborhood day spa near Prospect Park with sauna, steam room, cold plunge, and massage; day pass access, unrelated to the Bathhouse chain.
why: A solid, well-reviewed local bathhouse without the design profile or reach of the category leaders.

name: IcePass LA
who: Self-check-in cold plunge and Finnish sauna club across shared fitness-studio locations in LA; membership-based, unlimited access.
why: A lean, community-styled membership model for LA's cold-plunge boom, small but a genuine local following.

name: Bywater Sauna
who: Mobile barrel sauna and cold-plunge sessions on Seattle beaches (Golden Gardens, Alki, Leschi); pay-per-session or membership.
why: A grassroots beachside sauna-and-cold-water community built by the Coldwater Collective, small but a real local ritual and social hub.
